stem: A gaming backend stores session state by key with extremely high request rates and needs predictable low-latency lookups without SQL joins.

choices.text: Use Amazon Redshift as the transactional session-state store.
Use Amazon Neptune for flat key-value session retrieval.
Use Amazon OpenSearch Service as the source-of-truth transactional key store.
Use Amazon DynamoDB as the primary data store.

rationale: DynamoDB is optimized for key-based, low-latency, high-scale access patterns. Redshift is an analytic warehouse. Neptune targets graph relationships. OpenSearch Service targets search and analytics workloads rather than acting as the primary transactional key-value system of record.
